##  · G1-write-without-read — Should set_flags and process_map refuse write-without-read pages, like map_anon?

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 7

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

Decision references: docs/KERNEL-SPEC.md: R11 and the map_anon/set_flags/process_map Errors rows (Architect, settled rule), commit cf5465b85

Evidence: Merged in cf5465b85 with the Architect's R11 text. check_permissions, set_user_page_flags, user_frame (writable record must be readable) and a process_map row check refuse W-without-R before any state change; the legacy update_page_flags refuses it (MemoryInUse) and paging::Pte::leaf asserts W implies R, so a W-only boot segment fails closed. tests/write-only-attack passes on rv64 and rv32 with kernel verdicts; model mutation R11AllowsWriteOnly is caught via invariant I9 (100 mutations). Round-3 red team, simplifier and editor OK with notes; red team's final re-check confirmed every kernel path closed. Full bench green except the bench-ssh-loopback self-checks, which fail identically on the main tree (SELinux host). Residuals recorded in SWARM Review debt: mutation proven only through set_flags; process_map backs its source before the flags refusal.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `619e54ab8bed964ebab3fbaac921673d` · 2026-09-24T05:37:05Z

> G1 red team (assignment 4c1ad5c9) found that the kernel installs the reserved RISC-V encoding W-without-R through two runtime paths: set_flags(page, W) on a caller's own R|W page (kernel/src/mem.rs:1221-1241 -> arch/riscv/mem.rs:752, check_permissions rejects only empty and W|X), and process_map(child, ..., W) (kernel/src/process.rs:351-355). map_anon rejects W-without-R (mem.rs:1139-1143), matching its KERNEL-SPEC Errors row; the set_flags and process_map rows do not, and R11 does not forbid it. Consequence today: none within spec order, because read_record checks readable first. But user_frame's writable check does not imply readable, so any future single-pass record check would read a record the user cannot. Question: should the set_flags and process_map rows gain 'W without R' like map_anon, or should the spec state the encoding is allowed and unreadable? Red team recommends also requiring R whenever user_frame checks W. Nonblocking for G1; to be delivered to the Architect after the wash rebuild.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `8006ac1eb498f4e53cac475d4f967db3` · 2026-09-24T05:54:41Z

> Spec question from the G1 red team (clear review debt before the scheduler work), nonblocking; full evidence is in the thread's opening event. The kernel installs the reserved RISC-V W-without-R encoding through set_flags(page, W) and process_map(child, ..., W). map_anon refuses it and its KERNEL-SPEC Errors row says so; the set_flags and process_map rows do not, and R11 is silent. Should those rows gain "W without R" like map_anon, or should the spec state the encoding is allowed and unreadable? Give your recommendation and alternatives. If it is a genuine owner choice, raise a decision_request on this thread; otherwise cite the settled rule. Reply on this thread.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `1d408d8be73db0f340cac84cf5c98715` · 2026-09-24T05:57:59Z

> Settled rule, not an owner choice: no user mapping is ever writable without being readable, and every call that installs or changes permissions refuses W-without-R with InvalidArgument. No decision_request raised.
> 
> WHY IT IS SETTLED
> - The executable model, the conformance oracle, already applies one check_flags (flags 0, or W without R -> InvalidArgument) to map_anon, set_flags AND process_map (model/src/kernel.rs:544-550, called at 2369, 2389 and 2552). The spec's map_anon row documented it; the set_flags and process_map rows merely omitted it. The kernel accepting W-only in set_flags (kernel/src/mem.rs:1221-1241 via arch check_permissions) and process_map (kernel/src/process.rs:351-357) is therefore a kernel/model conformance gap, a finding, not a spec option.
> - TENETS 4 (ratified RISC-V specifications only) and "fail closed": the privileged architecture's PTE permission table marks XWR = 010 and 110 "reserved for future use", so installing it is not a defined, unreadable page; it is an unspecified encoding whose behaviour the ISA does not promise. The alternative "allowed and unreadable" would need a tenet amendment and cannot be specified against the ratified ISA, so it is not a live alternative.
> - R11 is the one statement of memory invariants; W^X was there and this sibling rule belongs beside it.
> 
> APPLIED (editorial consolidation under the QA protocol; no new approval needed; docs/KERNEL-SPEC.md only, unstaged, uncommitted):
> - R11 now reads: no mapping is writable and executable, and none is writable without being readable; the privileged architecture reserves that encoding, so map_anon, set_flags and process_map refuse it with InvalidArgument, and a writable user page is always readable.
> - Errors table: set_flags row now "InvalidArgument (range; flags 0, or W without R; a page not the caller's own mapping)"; process_map row now "... flags 0, or W without R ...". map_anon row unchanged. Check order unchanged (flags are checked where each row already lists "flags").
> 
> ALTERNATIVE considered and rejected: decode-time refusal of W-without-R (like W+X in libs/sys MemFlags::from_bits). Not chosen because W+X is refused at decode by an already-approved rule (ABI, Decoding) and changing the wire-level decoder for every caller is a bigger, unapproved change; the row-level kernel check matches the model exactly and is enough. If the orchestrator wants decode-time refusal as well, that is a small follow-on spec change I can make, but it is not required for consistency.
> 
> IMPLEMENTATION FOLLOW-UPS (not architect work; suggest folding into G1's review-debt fixes or K5's kernel-writer slot):
> 1. Kernel: refuse W-without-R in set_flags and process_map, matching map_anon. Simplest single place: arch check_permissions (kernel/src/arch/riscv/mem.rs:161) gains the readable requirement, since map_anon's map_run, set_flags and process_map all reach it; keep map_anon's explicit row check so neither rests on the other (the existing pattern for W+X).
> 2. Red team's user_frame point (arch/riscv/mem.rs:728-739): with the invariant in force, a writable user PTE is always readable, so a single-pass "writable" record check is sound. A debug assertion that W implies R in user_frame is cheap defence in depth; no spec change.
> 3. Tests: bench attack cases that set_flags(page, W) and process_map(child, ..., W) return InvalidArgument and leave the mapping/permissions unchanged; a model mutation "R11 set_flags/process_map allow W without R" alongside the existing R11SetFlagsAllowsWx so the checker proves the model's rule bites.
> 
> No other document references this rule. Returning the thread to the orchestrator; resolution needs the kernel fix and tests as evidence.
